newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Saudi considers setting up new industrial bank.
newsitem.headline: Saudi considers setting up new industrial bank.

text.p: A Saudi consulting company is studying the possibility of setting up a private industrial bank to help finance small and medium-scale private sector industries in the kingdom, a Saudi newspaper said on Sunday.

"The proposed industrial bank would be the first private bank of its kind in the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries and will cater for the needs of small and medium enterprises by providing them with loan finance," the daily Arab News said.
The GCC, a political and economic alliance, groups Bahrain, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Oman, the United Arab Emirates and Kuwait.
The Riyadh-based Consulting Centre for Finance and Investment was conducting the study for the Riyadh Chamber of Commerce and Industry.
Saudi Arabia's Industrial Development Fund is currently the main source of finance for industrial projects in the kingdom. It normally grants 50 percent of the total cost of the projects.
